route.rationale: installer prompt in install.sh and install.ps1, onboard plan JSON field, registry help

cells.title: Report the design offer in onboarding JSON and list --design-packs in onboard help
cells.action: Red first, and name EVERY new test with `design_offer` in it so one filter covers the cell. (1) In onboard/notices.rs, lift the predicate at lines 250-253 (`!picked && has_ui_file(repo_root)`, where picked means .bee/config.json has design.packs) into one `pub fn design_offer_due(repo_root: &Path) -> bool`, and make the existing notice code call it, so the DESIGN_PACKS_OFFER notice and the new field can never disagree. (2) In onboard/mod.rs, insert `design_offer` (a JSON boolean from design_offer_due) into the plan-mode payload beside `notices` (around line 496) and into the apply payload where it builds notices (around line 559). (3) In generated/registry_payload.json, add a `design-packs` string parameter to the `onboard` command's parameters.properties, described as: Design skill packs to install: a comma list of web, charts, motion, apple, figma, or none. Installs bee-design with the picked packs and records the pick; none removes them and stops the offer. Keep the file's existing formatting (one-line JSON) and check whether any test or `bee dev regen` derives or checks this file; if regen owns it, change the owner instead. Tests: design_offer is true for a repo with an index.html and no design pick; false for the same repo once .bee/config.json records design.packs (including an empty list or none); false for a repo with no UI file; and `bee onboard --help` output lists `--design-packs`. Do not change the DESIGN_PACKS_OFFER wording, the UI scan, or any existing assertion. No code comments.

truths: bee onboard --json reports design_offer true on a repo with a UI file and no recorded pick
design_offer is false once a pick is recorded, and false with no UI file

prohibitions: No change to DESIGN_PACKS_OFFER wording or the UI scan
No change to scripts/install.sh or scripts/install.ps1
No edit to any existing assertion

cells.title: Ask for design packs in both installers when onboarding offers them
cells.action: Red first, and name EVERY new test with `design` in it (the cell filter is `--test installer_contracts design`). dpi-1 adds a boolean `design_offer` to the `bee onboard --json` preview payload. In scripts/install.sh, right after the preview status check (around line 667-672) and BEFORE the dry-run exit: when DESIGN_PACKS is empty and `plan_field "$PREVIEW_JSON" design_offer` prints `true`: if ASSUME_YES is 0, DRY_RUN is 0 and can_prompt succeeds, print to /dev/tty one short plain question that names the five packs (web, charts, motion, apple, figma), says `none` stops the question, and that Enter skips; read the answer from /dev/tty. A non-empty answer sets DESIGN_PACKS, appends `--design-packs <answer>` to ONBOARD_FLAGS, and re-runs the preview with the same status check (onboarding refuses an unknown name before anything is written). Otherwise (--yes, no TTY, dry run, or Enter) log one plain line in the installer's `log` style, for a person, e.g. `design   this project has interface files; re-run with --design-packs web (or charts,motion,apple,figma, or none) to add design skills`. Never pick a pack for the user. Mirror the same behaviour in scripts/install.ps1: run the preview once with --json to read design_offer (keep the existing human preview output), ask with Read-Host only when not -Yes, not -DryRun and the console is interactive (reuse the test Confirm-Step already uses), otherwise Write-Host the plain line; keep install.ps1 pure ASCII. Tests in tests/installer_contracts.rs using run_install_sh: a sandbox host with an index.html and `-y` prints the plain line and installs no bee-design skill; with `--design-packs web` no line is printed; an interactive run under `script -qec` (skip the test when `script` is absent) answering `web` installs bee-design and bee-design-web and records the pick; a static test that install.ps1 reads design_offer and gates Read-Host on -Yes. Do not change other installer behaviour or any existing assertion. No code comments in the Rust test; shell and ps1 files keep their existing comment style. After the script edits, run the regen chain inside this cell (.bee/bin/bee dev regen) so the release manifest hashes the new install.sh and install.ps1.
cells.verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test installer_contracts design && .bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check

truths: An interactive install on a UI repo with no pick asks once and installs the answered packs
--yes, no TTY, or a dry run prints one plain line naming --design-packs and never blocks
A given --design-packs flag means no question and no line

artifacts.substantive: reads design_offer from the preview, asks or prints the line

key_links: both installers read design_offer from onboarding rather than scanning for UI files
prohibitions: No pack chosen without the user's answer
No read from the terminal under --yes, without a TTY, or on a dry run
No change to onboarding Rust code
No edit to any existing assertion
